description: Fourteen public-domain / CC0 documents by US federal teams (18F, CISA, USDS), each in the formats it travels in (original Word, Markdown or PDF; web page; Word; PDF export; Word HTML export; printed-and-scanned PDF). Every sentence or list item is labelled with its expected reading under a written policy. Three splits: dev (used to find and fix failures), held-out (labelled before XO ran on it; its failures were seen once, at the baseline, and never used to tune), and blind (labelled before any fix and measured once, at the end).
policy: step: an action in an ordered procedure (a numbered list or step table presented as a sequence) -> a capability, in order.
criterion: a checklist item (a check box, or an item under a heading that names a checklist) -> a constraint; a capability is a kind error.

rule: a statement with an explicit normative cue (must, required, expected to, need to, should, mandatory, never, do not, responsible for) -> a normative node; modality is checked only where the cue is unambiguous.
action: an instruction outside an ordered procedure (a plain imperative) -> a capability or a normative node; both are acceptable.
none: text that is neither normative nor an action (questions, placeholders, field labels, headings, link titles, descriptive or purpose statements); any output built from it is spurious.
opt: genuinely ambiguous text (permissions, label-value instructions, bracketed template guidance, code comments); neutral either way.
A numbered list under a "Checklist" heading is a checklist, not an ordered procedure.
